title: MicroSim Family Tree
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims
Learning Objects
Interactive Simulation

xAPI
description: A vis-network diagram that shows how a learning object, an interactive simulation, a MicroSim and an instrumented MicroSim specialize one another, with a quiz that asks learners to place unlabeled examples on the right level.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Kinds of learning objects and the property that distinguishes each
learningObjectives: The learner will classify an example as a learning object, an interactive simulation, a MicroSim, or an instrumented MicroSim, by identifying the property that distinguishes each level.
prerequisites: Definitions of learning object and interactive simulation (Chapter 1)

accessibility.notes: Info panel is an aria-live region; node colors are paired with text labels

controls.label: Quiz me / Explore
controls.purpose: Hide the box labels and start a four-example classification quiz, or return to explore mode

controls.label: Next example
controls.purpose: Advance the quiz after a correct placement

controls.label: Four level boxes
controls.purpose: Show a definition, an example and a near miss (explore) or place the example (quiz)

controls.label: Arrows
controls.purpose: Show the property each level adds

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Network explorer with click-to-inspect and a placement quiz
keyQuestions: What property does a MicroSim add to an interactive simulation?
Is a video with a metadata record an interactive simulation?
Why is every instrumented MicroSim also a learning object?
commonMisconceptions: Any animation counts as a simulation
Page-view analytics make a MicroSim instrumented
Any interactive program is a MicroSim
assessmentOpportunities: First-try accuracy in the placement quiz
Naming the missing property for a near miss
